subject: Urgent: ClearWave throughput regression — HOL lock & cache interference
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@clearwavehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production throughput drop — ClearWave

Ben / Redwood support,

We started seeing a sharp throughput drop and a spike in 500s on our ClearWave prod cluster around 08:40 PST. Latency p50s are stable but p95/p99 jumped from ~800ms to 4–6s and 5xxs are ~4.7% of requests. This started right after the model variant rollout you initiated this morning (v2.3-q4).

Impact: several customer-facing features are failing (document ingestion and summarization), and our ops team is getting alerts. We need immediate mitigation and a ETA for a fix — this is affecting our SLAs.

I can provide traces and sample request IDs. Please let me know if Redwood can pause the rollout or route our traffic to the previous serving variant.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Director, Platform Reliability
ClearWave Health

Attachment: request-ids.txt (text, 12 lines)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT — ClearWave prod regression (routing rollback in-flight)

Team — forwarding ClearWave's report. Rolling back their traffic now but we need a triage + mitigation plan. Initial observations from our front-line metrics:

- Sudden spike in KV cache evictions correlated with the rollout start (eviction rate x6).
- Batch queue depth increase on the model hosts serving ClearWave (p99 batch latency surged).
- Evidence of HOL-style head-of-line blocking: long-running batches appear to be preventing smaller latency-sensitive workloads from progressing.

Immediate asks:
1) Can we temporarily lower the KV eviction aggressiveness for ClearWave's tenant (config key: kv.eviction.threshold) to previous value and enable a longer TTL?
2) Can we divert ClearWave traffic to dedicated small-lane nodes (priority lane) for 1–2 hours while we stabilize?
3) If we need a hotfix, what's the rollback plan and estimated risk window?

Attached: perf_snapshot_20290610.json (sampling of metrics)

Ben

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT — ClearWave prod regression (routing rollback in-flight)

Quick diagnostic from ops: thanks for the snapshot. Key findings:

- KV eviction bursts: eviction_count spiked at rollout time; working set for ClearWave increased (prefix locality shift) which caused a noisy eviction spiral.
- Batch admission: our continuous batching logic allowed a few very large requests to accumulate; these created 3–5s batch processing windows that held KV locks, producing HOL blocking for small requests.
- Backpressure: downstream workers saw increased inflight tokens leading to transient 500s when request timeouts were hit.

Mitigation plan (can be executed within 20–40 minutes):
A) Immediate: revert ClearWave to v2.2 routing (in-flight) — already in progress.
B) Config adjustments (safe, reversible): reduce kv.eviction.aggressiveness to previous value (kv.eviction.threshold := 0.75 -> 0.9), extend per-tenant TTL by +30s, and lower max-batch-size for ClearWave to 32 tokens to limit large-batch latency.
C) Short-term traffic policing: move ClearWave to priority small-lane pool to isolate from noisy tenants (requires reallocating 2 small GPU nodes).
D) Follow-up: run a trace-based replay against staging with prefix distributions to ensure we don't re-trigger thrash.

I will prepare a rollback playbook (hotfix_playbook_rollback.md) and a runbook snippet for operators. Risks: slight throughput reduction while lowering batch sizes; acceptable given SLA impact.

Rishi
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Ben

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production throughput drop — ClearWave (post-mitigation summary)

Sara / team — follow-up after the mitigation window. Timeline + outcome summary: 

- 06/10 09:35 — Incident reported.
- 06/10 09:45 — Routing rollback to v2.2 completed for ClearWave.
- 06/10 10:20 — Config adjustments applied (kv eviction threshold rollback, batch size cap).
- 06/10 11:30 — Traffic shifted to small-lane pool; p99 dropped from ~5.2s to ~1.1s; 5xxs reduced to 0.3%.

Current status: system stable for ClearWave, error rates back to acceptable range, but the root cause analysis points to a combination of prefix distribution change (customer workload) plus our more aggressive eviction settings exposed during the model variant behavior. The recommended next steps:

1) Formal RCA with replay test (OPS-1745) and model variant rollout guardrails for tenants with skewed prefix patterns.
2) Permanent conservative default for kv.eviction.aggressiveness and a targeted canary schedule for model variants that touch prefix locality.
3) Update the rollout checklist and add a preflight for per-tenant working set estimation.

Note: ClearWave indicated they may escalate contract terms if similar incidents repeat. I've looped in leadership for visibility. We should prioritize the RCA and the safe-rollout work.

Attachments: hotfix_playbook_rollback.md (operator steps), perf_snapshot_20290610.json

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
